data.one_liner: Provides BLoC to descendant widgets with O(1) access and automatic disposal.
data.what_it_does: bloc_provider lets you create a BLoC instance and expose it to the widget subtree. The provided BLoC is retrieved in O(1) time and is disposed automatically when the provider's state is removed.
use_when: You need a lightweight way to share a BLoC across widgets without adding a large dependency
You prefer O(1) lookup and automatic disposal of the BLoC
Your project already uses the classic BLoC pattern and wants a simple provider
avoid_when: You require a actively maintained package with richer features
You need code‑generation, scoped providers, or advanced state‑management capabilities
You are already using Riverpod, Provider, or flutter_bloc for state management
weaknesses: Minimally maintained and may lack future updates
Limited feature set compared to newer providers
No built‑in support for code‑gen or advanced scoping

alternatives.name: provider
alternatives.why_pick_it: Widely used, actively maintained, and supports simple dependency injection

alternatives.name: bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: Full BLoC library with extensive tooling and community support

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: Modern, compile‑time safety and richer provider features

data.minimal_example:
void main()=>runApp(BlocProvider<CounterBloc>(creator:(_,__)=>CounterBloc(),child:MyApp()));
class MyApp extends StatelessWidget{ @override Widget build(BuildContext c){final bloc=BlocProvider.of<CounterBloc>(c);return MaterialApp(home:Scaffold(body:StreamBuilder<int>(stream:bloc.count,initialData:bloc.count.value,builder:(_,s)=>Text('count: ${s.data}'))),floatingActionButton:FloatingActionButton(onPressed:()=>bloc.increment.add(null),child:Icon(Icons.add)),);}}
